note: The retirement law every one of the seven typed-operation publication lanes obeys once its own store has REJECTED it (a superseding mutation moved the store past the generation the publication captured). A rejected publication drains its rejection reason one scalar per bounded turn, so the turns before the terminal one are ordinary retirement progress, NOT faults: answering them with an error re-raised the same rejection on every turn and the host saw `typed-operation failed: <lane> publication is retiring a rejected authority` forever instead of a publication that retires. The rejection surfaces exactly once, at the terminal turn. Window-transient is the one lenient lane: its authority is per-window ephemeral state the next turn re-captures against the live generation, so a cleanly retired superseded publication owes the host nothing. Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language must answer these exact rows.

lanes.rejectedFault: artifact-store publication rejected stale or cancelled authority
lanes.falseTerminalFault: artifact-store publication closed without terminal emptiness

windowTransientReBegin.note: After the rejected publication has fully retired, the SAME window must become publishable again. The authority captured at command admission is stale by construction — the superseding write moved the partition generation — so the publication site must refresh it against the live generation before it begins, which is exactly what the window-transient emission branch does before `begin`.
